title: Topic 12 · The Importance of Self-Esteem · Chunks
source: Modern Wisdom · Chris Williamson & Naval Ravikant · youtu.be/KyfUysrNaco

items.s: The worst outcome in the world is not having self-esteem.
I look at the people who don’t like themselves and that’s the toughest slot because they’re always wrestling with themselves.

It’s hard enough to face the outside world, and no one’s going to like you more than you like yourself, so if you’re struggling with yourself then the outside world becomes an insurmountable challenge.

items.zh: 也可能只是环境造成的
items.s: It might be genetic, it might just be circumstantial.

items.zh: 小时候被无条件地爱着
items.s: A lot of times I think it’s because they just weren’t unconditionally loved as a child and that sort of seeps in at a deep core level, but self-esteem issues can be the most limiting.
One interesting thought is that to some extent self-esteem is a reputation you have with yourself.

items.c: a reputation you have with yourself
items.s: One interesting thought is that to some extent self-esteem is a reputation you have with yourself.
You’re watching yourself at all times, you know what you’re doing and you have your own moral code.
If I look back on my life and what are the moments that I’m actually proud of, they’re very far and few between.
It’s when I made a sacrifice for somebody or something that I loved.
Now that’s through an explicit mental exercise, but I’ll bet you at some level I’m recording that implicitly.

items.c: the way to create love is to give love
items.zh: 创造爱的方式就是给予爱
items.s: So that tells me that even if I am not being loved, the way to create love is to give love, to express love through sacrifice and through duty.
It’s like, yeah, but that was you sacrificing something that you wanted less for something that you wanted more, as opposed to genuinely taking some sort of cost.
